block.legworks.hydraulic_leg_mount.toolt: _Faster_ rotation changes the Reach _faster_. Without power it _Softens fully_ and lets the Ship settle.
_Softens_ the Leg: a stronger signal makes it _softer_.
The Leg is _inert_. _Link_ it by clicking it with a Leg Controller.
A powered _Leg Mount_. It Levels to the _Ride Height_ of its _Leg Controller_ and folds on _Gear Up_. Set _Stiffness_ and _Damping_ on its sides.
block.legworks.leg_controller.tooltip.be: _Links_ them, up to _8 Legs_ within _16 blocks_. _Sneak-click_ a placed Controller first to select it.
_Gear Up_: the Leg Group folds against the Ship. No signal means _Gear Down_.
Sets the _Ride Height_, how high the Legs hold the deck. _Auto_ uses each Limb's default.
block.legworks.leg_controller.tooltip.su: Coordinates a _Leg Group_ of Hydraulic Legs on the _same Ship_. Needs no rotational power.
The Leg _reaches down_ to the Ground and keeps the deck level, with _fixed_ Stiffness and Damping.
It is a _Bumper_: a spring against Ground it meets. It never Levels.
_Fits_ the Limb. _Sneak-click_ with an empty hand to take it back.
A _Leg Mount_ for Ships. Fit a _Limb_ and it _Levels_ the Ship on its own. Needs no power and no Leg Controller.

item.legworks.heavy_limb.tooltip.summary: A sturdy _Limb_ for big, heavy Ships. _Reach 3.5 blocks_, _Stiffness x2_: it sags half as much.

item.legworks.long_limb.tooltip.summary: A long brass _Limb_ for tall Ships and rough Ground. _Reach 4.5 blocks_, _Stiffness x1_.
item.legworks.short_limb.tooltip.behavio: _Fits_ onto it and becomes the leg drawn below the Mount. Any Limb fits any Leg Mount.

legworks.jei.fitting.hint: R-Click the Leg Mount with the Limb
legworks.jei.info.controller: Coordinates the Hydraulic Legs Linked to it (a Leg Group). It needs no rotational power and must be on the same Ship as its Legs.
legworks.jei.info.controller_gear: Gear Up: any redstone signal folds the Leg Group against the Ship for flight. Without a signal the Legs come back down (Gear Down).
legworks.jei.info.controller_linking: Linking: sneak-click the placed Leg Controller with a Leg Controller item to select it, then click each Hydraulic Leg Mount. Up to 8 Legs within 16 blocks. Click a Linked Leg again to unlink it.
legworks.jei.info.controller_ride_height: Ride Height: scroll its value box to set how high the Legs hold the deck, in blocks. Auto uses each Limb's own default height.
legworks.jei.info.facing: Facing: the Limb extends the way the Mount faces. Facing down it is a Foot and helps Level the Ship. Facing sideways or up it is a Bumper: a spring against Ground it meets, never Leveling.
legworks.jei.info.goggles: Engineer's Goggles show each Leg's Reach, load and settings, and warn about Overreach and Conflicting Ride Height.
legworks.jei.info.hydraulic: Place it on a Ship's hull and right-click it with a Limb. It needs rotation through its shaft (4 SU per RPM) and a Linked Leg Controller on the same Ship; without a Link it is inert.
legworks.jei.info.hydraulic_power: Power: faster rotation changes the Reach faster (a full Gear Up takes about 4 s at 16 RPM). Without power, or when overstressed, the Leg Softens fully and lets the Ship settle onto the Ground.
legworks.jei.info.hydraulic_settings: Stiffness (25 to 200 percent) and Damping (0.2 to 1.5) are set on the value boxes on its sides. Stiffness is how hard the spring pushes back. Damping is how quickly it stops bouncing.
legworks.jei.info.hydraulic_softening: Softening: a redstone signal on its top face makes the Leg softer; a stronger signal means softer.
legworks.jei.info.limb: A Limb fits any Leg Mount: right-click the Mount with it. It becomes the Leg drawn below the Mount. Sneak-click the Mount with an empty hand to take the Limb back.
legworks.jei.info.limb_overreach: If the Ground is too uneven for the Reach, the Legs stretch to the maximum and the Ship tilts toward the low side: Overreach.
legworks.jei.info.limb_stats: The Limb decides the Leg's maximum Reach and base Stiffness. Reach: %s blocks. Stiffness: x%s. Default height: %s blocks.
legworks.jei.info.simple: Place it on a Ship's hull and right-click it with a Limb. It needs no power and no Leg Controller: it Levels the Ship on its own, with fixed Stiffness and Damping, at the Limb's default height. Off a Ship it does nothing.

legworks.ponder.hydraulic_leg_power.head: Powering Hydraulic Legs
legworks.ponder.hydraulic_leg_power.text: Hydraulic Legs need rotational power. Without it they are fully Softened and the Ship rests on the Ground
Power them through the shaft (4 SU per RPM). Faster rotation changes the Reach faster
If power is lost or the network is overstressed, the Legs Soften fully and the Ship settles
They also need a Linked Leg Controller on the same Ship. Unlinked, they stay inert
Stiffness (25 to 200 percent): how hard the Leg's spring pushes back. Higher Stiffness sags less
Damping (0.2 to 1.5): how quickly a bounce dies down. Low Damping rocks, high Damping settles fast
The top of a Hydraulic Leg Mount is the face opposite its Limb. A redstone signal there Softens the Leg
Softened Legs push back less, so the Ship sinks toward the Ground. A stronger signal makes them softer
Use an Analog Lever for partial Softening, e.g. to kneel a parked Ship for loading
Remove the signal and the Legs lift the Ship back to its Ride Height
legworks.ponder.leg_controller_linking.h: Linking Legs to a Leg Controller
legworks.ponder.leg_controller_linking.t: A Leg Controller coordinates the Hydraulic Legs on its Ship. It needs no rotational power
Sneak-click the placed Leg Controller with a Leg Controller item to select it
Then click each Hydraulic Leg to Link it. Click a Linked Leg again to unlink it
Up to 8 Legs within 16 blocks, all on the same Ship. A Leg belongs to one Controller at a time
You can also click the Legs first and then place the Controller: they are Linked as it is placed. Linking works before the Ship is assembled
legworks.ponder.leg_controller_ride_heig: Scroll the Leg Controller's value to set the Ride Height: how high its Legs hold the deck
Auto, the default, holds each Leg at its Limb's own height. Several Controllers on one Ship settle in between
A redstone signal on the Leg Controller folds its Legs against the Ship for flight: Gear Up
Without a signal the Legs unfold again, ready for Landing: Gear Down. Higher RPM folds them faster
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_facing.text_1: A Leg Mount facing down is a Foot. Feet carry the Ship and take part in Leveling
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_facing.text_2: Facing sideways or up it is a Bumper: a spring that pushes back from Ground it meets. Bumpers never Level
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_facing.text_3: Mounts face the side you place them on. Sneak while placing to flip them, or turn them with a Wrench
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_fitting.heade: Fitting a Limb to a Leg Mount
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_fitting.text_: Leg Mounts are placed on the hull of a Ship. Without a Limb they do nothing
Right-click it with a Limb to fit it. The Limb becomes the Leg below the Mount
Any Limb fits any Leg Mount. The Limb decides the Leg's maximum Reach and its Stiffness
Sneak-click with an empty hand to take the Limb back
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_leveling.head: Leveling on uneven Ground
legworks.ponder.simple_leg_leveling.text: Simple Legs Level a Ship on their own. They need no power and no Leg Controller
Each Leg finds its own Reach down to the Ground, so the deck stays level
Feet grip the Ground like rubber pads, so a Ship does not slide off a slope
If the Ground is too uneven for the Limbs' Reach, the Legs stretch to their maximum and the Ship tilts toward the low side: Overreach
Longer Limbs, or a Ride Height closer to the middle of the Reach, give the Legs more room
legworks.ponder.tag.legs.description: Leg Mounts, Limbs and Leg Controllers that land Ships on uneven Ground and keep them level
legworks.status.overreach: Overreach: Ground too uneven to level
